Joint F Tests of Contrasts among Means (Slices)

Source: R/pm_joint.R
pm_joint.Rd

F tests of sets of contrasts among the predicted means of a model term. With by, the means of the term are compared within each level of the by factor(s): the test of nitro within each Variety, as SAS LSMEANS nitro*Variety / SLICE=Variety or emmeans::joint_tests(model, by = "Variety"). With ctrmatrix, all its rows are tested together.

Usage

pm_joint(model, modelterm, by = NULL, ctrmatrix = NULL,
         df_method = c("auto", "Kenward-Roger", "Satterthwaite", "containment", "between-within", "KR-SAS"),
         weights = c("equal", "proportional", "outer", "cells", "flat"), vcov = NULL)

Arguments

model

A fitted model, as for predictmeans.

modelterm

Name (in "quotes") of the model term whose means are compared, e.g. "nitro:Variety".

by

Optional name(s) of factor(s) of modelterm: test the differences among the means within each of their levels. Without by and ctrmatrix, all differences among the means of modelterm are tested.

ctrmatrix

Optional contrast matrix over the means of modelterm (as for contrastmeans, e.g. from contrast_family or specify_contrast); its rows are tested together.

df_method

For lmer models ("between-within" also for lme and gls): the denominator df (see Details).

weights

How the means average over other factors, as in predictmeans.

vcov

Optional covariance of the coefficients, as in predictmeans: the F statistic is then the Wald F with this covariance, and the denominator df those of the model's own test.

Value

A data frame with one row per test: the by levels (if any), df1, df2, F.ratio and p.value. Attribute "df_method" says how df2 was found.

Details

The F statistic and its denominator degrees of freedom follow the model:

lmer

Kenward-Roger (the default for REML fits): the scaled F test of Kenward and Roger (1997), as pbkrtest::KRmodcomp() and the ANOVA tables of this package; Satterthwaite (the default for ML fits): as lmerTest::contest(joint = TRUE); containment: the Wald F with the containment df of modelterm.

KR-SAS

(lmer) as Kenward-Roger, with the observed information of the variance parameters (SAS DDFM=KR; see predictmeans).

between-within

(lmer, lme, gls) the Wald F with the between-within df of modelterm (SAS DDFM=BETWITHIN; see predictmeans).

lme, gls with df_method = "Satterthwaite", "Kenward-Roger" or "KR-SAS"

as for lmer (Satterthwaite df of the F test, lmerTest's rule).

lme

the Wald F with the smallest nlme df of modelterm and its factors (as contrastmeans).

other models

the Wald F with the residual df (normal-based when there is none).

Contrasts that are linear combinations of others are dropped, so df1 is the rank of the set. emmeans::joint_tests() gives a slightly different Kenward-Roger test (the unscaled F with its own df).

References

Kenward, M. G. and Roger, J. H. (1997), Small sample inference for fixed effects from restricted maximum likelihood, Biometrics, 53, 983-997.

Author

Dongwen Luo, Siva Ganesh and John Koolaard

Examples

  library(predictmeans)
  Oats$nitro <- factor(Oats$nitro)
  fm <- lmer(yield ~ nitro*Variety + (1|Block/Variety), data = Oats)
  # nitrogen within each variety (SAS SLICE)
  pm_joint(fm, "nitro:Variety", by = "Variety")
#>       Variety df1 df2   F.ratio      p.value
#> 1 Golden Rain   3  45 13.022765 2.969047e-06
#> 2  Marvellous   3  45  9.952878 3.769265e-05
#> 3     Victory   3  45 15.315709 5.256928e-07
  # varieties within each nitrogen level
  pm_joint(fm, "nitro:Variety", by = "nitro")
#>   nitro df1      df2   F.ratio   p.value
#> 1     0   2 30.23076 1.2245400 0.3080589
#> 2   0.2   2 30.23076 1.8814476 0.1697812
#> 3   0.4   2 30.23076 0.2156336 0.8072596
#> 4   0.6   2 30.23076 0.4010511 0.6731259
  # a set of contrasts: linear and quadratic nitrogen trends together
  pm_joint(fm, "nitro", ctrmatrix = contrast_family(Kmatrix(fm, "nitro"), "poly", max.degree = 2))
#>   df1 df2  F.ratio      p.value
#> 1   2  45 56.51839 5.311565e-13
